questions.question: Which of the following rivers originates from the 'Rakas Lake'?

The correct answer is __**Sutlej**__.

__
 
• **Sutlej river **__originates from the 'Rakas Lake'.
 
• The origin of the Sutlej River is located close to Lake Rakas tal in Tibet in the vicinity of the Kailash Mountain Range.
 
• The waters of the Satluj River are distributed to India according to the Indus Waters Treaty between Pakistan and India
 
• There are various hydroelectric power and irrigation projects over the river like the Kol Dam, Bhakra Nangal Dam, Baspa Hydroelectric Power Project, and Nathpa Jhakri Project.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question: Through which of the following states does the Rushikulya river pass?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Rushikulya River** is one of the **major rivers **in the state of **Odisha**.

 
 
• It covers the entire catchment area in the **districts **of **Kandhamal **and **Ganjam district **of Odisha.
 
• The **Rushikulya originates **at an **elevation **of about **1000 metres** from the **Daringbadi hills **of the **Eastern Ghats **range.
 
• The place from where the river **originates**, **Daringbadi **is called the ‘ **Kashmir of Odisha**.‘
 
• It **meets **the** Bay of Bengal** at **Puruna Bandha **in **Ganjam**.
 
• Its **tributaries **are the **Bagua**, the **Dhanei**, the **Badanadi **etc.
 
• It has** no delta **as such at its mouth.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a tributary of river Kaveri?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Musi**__.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Musi river** is not a tributary of the river Kaveri.
 
• **It is a tributary of the Krishna River, which is another major river in Southern India.**
 
• The Musi River is primarily located in the** Telangana state of India.**
 
• It passes through **the city of Hyderabad and is known for its historical significance in the city's development.**
 
• The river is infamous for causing one of the worst floods in** Hyderabad's history, known as the Great Musi Flood of 1908.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhavani:**

 
 
• The** Bhavani River is a significant tributary of the Kaveri River, originating from the Western Ghats in Tamil Nadu.**
 
• It is the **second-longest river in Tamil Nadu and contributes significantly to the water volume of the Kaveri River.**
 
 
 
• **Hemavati:**
 
 
• The **Hemavati River is another important tributary of the Kaveri River.**
 
• It originates from the **Western Ghats in Karnataka and joins the Kaveri River at Krishnarajasagara.**
 
 
 
• **Kabini:**
 
 
• The **Kabini River, also known as Kapila, is a significant tributary of the Kaveri River.**
 
• It originates in **Kerala and flows eastward to join the Kaveri River in Karnataka.**
 
• The **Kabini River is known for the Kabini Forest Reserve, a popular wildlife destination.**

questions.question: Which river of India drains into Bay of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Godavari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Godavari**

 
 
• The Godavari is India's largest peninsular river.
 
• It is the second-longest river in India after the Ganga.
 
• It rises from Maharashtra's Thriambak hill.
 
• Its length is about **1465** km.
 
• Due to its length and the area it covers, it is also known as the ‘Dakshin Ganga’.
 
• Flows through the states of Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mahi

 
 
• ​It originates in the Mahi Kanta hills, from the northern slopes of Vindhyas at an altitude of 500 m near village Bhopawar, Sardarpur Tehsil in the Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It flows through the Vagad region of Rajasthan, enters Gujarat, and flows into the Arabian Sea.
 
 
 
• **​Narmada**
 
 
• The Narmada river originates from the Narmada Kund located in Amarkantak, Anuppur district in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• Amarkantak is located on the Maikal mountain. 
 
• The Narmada river forms the unmarked boundary between North and South India.
 
• The major tributaries of the Narmada are Barna, Tawa, Kanar, Kolar, Man, Hatni, Uri, Shakkar, etc.
 
• It flows westwards (1, 312 km) before falling into the Gulf of Khambhat.
 
• The Narmada river is the longest river in Madhya Pradesh and it's called "The Lifeline of Madhya Pradesh".
 
• The waterfalls created by the Narmada River include Kapil Dhara and Dudh Dhara Falls (Anuppur), Dhuandhar Falls (Bhedaghat, Jabalpur), Sahasradhara Falls (Maheshwar, Khargone), Dardhi Falls, Manadhata Falls, etc.
 
 

 
• **Tapi**

 
 
• The Tapti River (aka Tapi river )is a river in central India located to the south of the Narmada river which flows westwards before draining into the Arabian Sea.
 
• The river has a length of around 724 kms and flows through the states of Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh.
 
• Tapti river originates from Multai Betul district Madhya Pradesh. And also from the Satpura range.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f688b6475db419260362a92565c08925f5fa46206569f5165b7748c6e68c00ce.png] 

66:T

questions.question: Where does Alaknanda River join Bhagirathi River in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Devprayag.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Alaknanda River joins the Bhagirathi River at** Devprayag **in the Indian state of **Uttarakhand.**
 
• Devprayag is located in the **Tehri Garhwal district **of Uttarakhand, India.
 
• This confluence marks the beginning of the holy river **Ganga**, which flows downstream through the** plains of India.**
 
• Devprayag is considered one of the **Panch Prayag** (five confluences) in Uttarakhand, which holds immense** religious significance** for Hindus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prayagraj**

 
 
• It is formerly known as** Allahabad**, is a city located in the northern state of **Uttar Pradesh, India.**
 
• It is situated at the confluence of three sacred rivers **(Triveni Sangam), the Ganges, the Yamuna, and the mythical Saraswati.**
 
• Prayagraj is famous for hosting the **Kumbh Mela, **the largest religious gathering in the world.
 
 
 
• **Champawat**
 
 
• It is a district of the northern Indian state of** Uttarakhand.**
 
• It was **once the capital of the Kumaon Kingdom.**
 
• The **Baleshwar Temple,** dedicated to Lord Shiva, is a prominent attraction and other notable temples of Champawat include **the Kranteshwar Mahadev Temple and the Nagnath Temple.**
 
• This district also has **Champawat Wildlife Sanctuary and the Nanda Devi National Park.**
 
 
 
• **​Dehradun**
 
 
• It serves as the** capital city** of the Indian state of** Uttarakhand.**
 
• Dehradun acts as a gateway to popular hill stations like** Mussoorie and Dhanaulti,** offering breathtaking views and a pleasant climate.
 
• Dehradun houses institutions such as the **Indian Military Academy (IMA)** and various government offices, contributing to its importance in defence and administration.
 
• The city is renowned for its prestigious educational institutions, including top **boarding schools **and the **Forest Research Institute.**

questions.question: _______ is a tributary of river Godavari.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Indravati**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The Godavari river is the largest river system in Peninsular India.
 
• The Godavari basin extends over the States of Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha in addition to smaller parts in Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, and Puducherry (Yanam).
 
• The other names for the Godavari River are The Vriddh (Old) Ganga or the Dakshin (South) Ganga.
 
• Godavari river drains into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Godavari river originates from Bramhagiri mountains at Trimbakeshwar.
 
• Tributaries: Pravara, Purna, Manjira, Penganga, Wardha, Wainganga, Pranhita (combined flow of Wainganga, Penganga, Wardha), Indravati, Maner, and the Sabri.
 
• The longest tributary- The Manjira
 
• The largest tributary- The Pranhita

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bcf92b48b809c3eb721c9fed87b753c04217e0130f42e4de80a9af2dcc680ed2.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Chambal:**

__
 
• The Chambal river originates in Manpura near Indore in Madhya Pradesh.__
 
• The length of the river is 900 km and it is a tributary of the Yamuna river.
 
• The Chambal River remains one of North India’s unpolluted rivers, home to a rich diversity of flora and fauna.
 
• The National Chambal Gharial Wildlife Sanctuary is famous for the rare Ganges river dolphin.
 
• Apart from the Ganges river dolphin, the other inhabitants of the sanctuary include magar (crocodile) and gharial (alligator). Migratory birds from Siberia form part of its rich avian fauna.

**Banas:**

__
 
• Banas river originates from Khamnor Hills of the Aravalli Range, near Kumbhalgarh in Rajsamand, Rajasthan. '
 
• Banas river is a tributary of the Chambal River and ii is approximately 512 kilometers in length.
 
• This river is also called ‘Van Ki Asha‘.
 
• There is another river in Rajasthan with name of Banas.
 
• The Banas river entirely flows within the Rajasthan in:-
 
 
• Ajmer, Bhilwara, Bundi, Chittorgarh, Dausa, Jaipur, Pali, Rajsamand, Sawai Madhopur, Sirohi, Tonk, and Udaipur districts of Rajasthan. 
 
 
 
• It flows northeast through the Mewar region of Rajasthan and meets the Chambal near the village of Rameshwar in Sawai Madhopur district.

**Tawa:**

 
• Tawa River is the tributary of the Narmada River__.
 
• It is the longest tributary of the Narmada River.
 
• Its origin is in the Satpura range.
 
• It meets the Narmada at Hoshangabad district.
 
• Its length is 172 km.

questions.question: Which among the following pairs of rivers and tributaries is incorrect?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The incorrect pair of rivers and tributaries from the options is: **Chambal - Rapti**
 
• **Chambal River **is not a tributary of the** Rapti River.**
 
• The **Chambal River **is a major river in** central India**, and it is not a **tributary of the Rapti River**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yamuna - Tons:**

 
 
• **The Yamuna River** is a major river in **northern India** and is one of the** longest tributaries of the Ganges River.**
 
• **The Tons River** is a** tributary of the Yamuna River**.
 
• It flows through the **Indian states of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh** before joining the **Yamuna River near Dehradun**.
 
 
 
• **Godavari - Manjira:**
 
 
• **The Godavari River** is the** second-longest river in India** and flows through the** states of Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Odisha. **
 
• **The Manjira River** is a major tributary of the **Godavari River.**
 
• It originates in the** Balaghat Range in Maharashtra and flows through Telangana before joining the Godavari River near Medak.**
 
 
 
• **Indus - Jhelum:**
 
 
• **The Indus River** is one of the** longest rivers in Asia and flows through China, India, and Pakistan.**
 
• **The Jhelum River** is a **tributary of the Indus River.**
 
• It originates in the **Himalayas in Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir** and flows through **Pakistan before joining the Indus River near the city of Trimmu.**

__

questions.question: Which river in India flows through a rift valley?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Narmada.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **T****he Narmada and the Tapi** are the major rivers in India that flow through **rift valleys**. 
 
• The Narmada originates on the western flank of the Amarkantak plateau at a height of about 1,057 m.
 
• The other rivers which flow through the rift valley include the **Damodar River** in Chota Nagpur Plateau and Tapti
 
• The **Tapti River and Mahi River **also flow through rift valleys, but between different ranges.
 
• There are **three** rivers in India that flow through a rift valley. The two other rivers which flow through a rift valley are Damodar and Narmada.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• A rift valley is **a lowland region that forms where Earth's tectonic plates move apart or rift**.
 
• Rift valleys are found both on land and at the bottom of the ocean, where they are created by the process of seafloor spreading.
 
• The linear depression may subsequently be further deepened by the forces of erosion
 
• In India **on the southern slopes of the Vindhyachal mountain ranges, at the Malwa plateau escarpment boundary** is formed, under which the rift valley is formed and the Narmada river flows in this valley in the west direction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Periyar river is the longest river in Kerala. 

 
 
• It is popularly known as the lifeline of Kerala.
 
• The length of the Periyar river is 244 km.
 
• It originates from Sivagiri Hills in the Western Ghats and empties into Kodungallur lake.
 
• It passes through two states: Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
 
• The major Tributaries are:
 
 
• Muthirapuzha River
 
• Mullayar River
 
• Cheruthoni River
 
• Perinjankutti River
 
• Edamala River
 
 
 
 
 
• The Penganga River is a tributary of the **Wardha River**, which is a tributary of the Pranhita River, which flows into the **Godavari**.
 
• Son river originates from the Amarkantak plateau in the Anuppur district of Madhya Pradesh.
 
 
• It flows through Madhya Pradesh, Chhatisgarh, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and finally joins Ganga in Bihar near Patna.
 
• Ghaghra, Johilla, Chhoti Mahanadi, Gopad, Rihand, Kanhar, and North Koel are the tributaries of the Son river.
 
• The Bansagar Dam in Madhya Pradesh is also on the Son river.

questions.question: Which is the biggest tributary of the upper Brahmaputra that originates in the Tibetan Himalayas and winds its way into India through Arunachal Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Subansiri.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Subansiri **is the biggest tributary of the **upper Brahmaputra.**
 
• It originates in the** Tibetan Himalayas** and flows through **Arunachal Pradesh** before joining the **Brahmaputra in Assam.**
 
• The Brahmaputra River is one of the major rivers in Asia, flowing through **China, India, and Bangladesh.**
 
• It is also known as the **Tsangpo-Brahmaputra River** system.
 
• Some of the other tributaries of the Brahmaputra include the** Lohit, Dibang, and Kameng rivers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A tributary of the** Krishna River **is the** Yerala River.**

 
 
• It comes from the far north of **Khatav taluka in Satara district,** near the Mhaskoba highlands.
 
 
 
• The **Musi River** flows through **Telangana, India**, and is a significant tributary of the Krishna River in the Deccan Plateau.
 
 
• **Hyderabad** is located along the Musi River's banks.
 
 
 
• One of the rivers that flows through the T**apti River Basin** is the **Aner River.**
 
 
• It is situated in the Indian state of **Maharashtra**, close to Hisale.
 
 
 
• The Brahmaputra river basin is home to a diverse range of **flora and fauna**, including the endangered Gangetic dolphin and the one-horned rhinoceros.
 
• The Brahmaputra River is an important source of water for** irrigation, fishing, transportation, and hydropower generation** in the northeastern region of India.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers flows into the Bay of Bengal ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **River Krishna**__:

 __
 
• The river extends over the states of Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Karnataka and finally empties into** Bay of Bengal**.
 
• **Krishna river originates in the Western Ghats near Mahabaleshwar.**
 
• Ghatprabha, Malprabha, Tungabhadra, Bhima, and Musi are the few important tributaries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Indus rises near** Mansarovar in Tibet** and flows through India, and thereafter through Pakistan before draining into the Arabian Sea.

 
 
• Major tributaries of the Indus River are **Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej.**

 
 
• **Sutlej**:

 
 
• It is the longest of the five tributaries of the Indus River.
 
• It is sometimes known as the Red River.
 
• The Sutlej finally drains into the Indus in Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Beas**:
 
 
• The Beas River rises in the Himalayas in central Himachal Pradesh, India, and meets the Satluj river at Harike in Punjab.
 
 
 
• **Ravi**:
 
 
• It is one of the five tributaries of the Indus River.
 
• It is a transboundary river crossing northwestern India and eastern Pakistan.

questions.question: Lohit river is a tributary of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __Brahmaputra__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Lohit River:**

 
 
• It is a river in China and India.
 
• The Lohit River is also known as the Zayu River.
 
• **Lohit River is a tributary to the Brahmaputra River. Hence, Option 4 is correct.**

questions.question: Which of the following rivers originates from the Milam Glacier in Uttarakhand?

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary factor contributing to the dryness of old wells?

options.text: A lot of boring pumps have been set up in the adjacent areas.
The ground surrounding the wells has been covered with a layer of vegetation,

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A lot of boring pumps have been set up in the adjacent areas.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Primary factor contributing to dryness of old wells:**

 
 
• A lot of boring pumps have been set up in the adjacent areas, leading to depletion of groundwater resources and drying up of old wells.
 
• Groundwater depletion is a major issue in many parts of the world due to increasing population and demand for water.
 
• Wells being covered may contribute to their abandonment, but not necessarily to their dryness.
 
• People stopping to utilize wells may be a consequence of their dryness, not the cause.
 
• Vegetation around wells may actually help retain moisture and prevent evaporation, but it is not the primary factor contributing to their dryness. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Boring pumps extract groundwater from aquifers, which are underground layers of permeable rock or soil that hold water.
 
• Overuse of groundwater resources can lead to depletion and even collapse of aquifers, causing wells to dry up.
 
• Groundwater depletion can also have other negative impacts, such as land subsidence, saltwater intrusion, and reduced streamflow.
 
• In some cases, old wells can be rehabilitated by deepening or re-drilling them, or by implementing sustainable groundwater management practices.

questions.question: Which river basin covers an area of 65,145 km², of which about 80% liesin Maharashtra?

 **The Godavari** originates in the Western Ghats of central India near Nashik in Maharashtra, from the Arabian Sea.

questions.question: Which of the following river originates in Rajasthan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Banas__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Banas river originates from the state of Rajasthan__.

 __
 
• The river originates from the Khamnor hills of the Aravali range near Kumbhalgarh.
 
• It is also known as 'Van ki Asha' (Hope of forest).
 
• It flows northeast through the Mewar region of Rajasthan and meets the Chambal near the village of Rameshwar in Sawai Madhopur district.
 
• Berach and Menali are the right bank tributaries of the Banas river.
 
• Kothari, Khari, Dai, Dheel River, Sohadara River, Morel, and Kalisil are the left bank tributaries of Banas river.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chambal River

 
 
• It is the tributary of the Yamuna River.
 
• It rises in the Vindhyachal range South of Mhow, the western state of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It flows from the north into the southeastern state of Rajasthan.
 
• It ends on the confluence of five rivers which includes the Chambal, Kwari, Yamuna, Sind, Pahuj, at Pachnada near Bhareh in Uttar Pradesh, at the border of Bhind and Etawah districts.
 
• Major Tributary - Kshipra, Kalisindh, Parvati, Bansa, Newaj, Kwari, Sindh, etc.
 
 
 
• Narmada River
 
 
• It originates from the Narmada Kund located in Amarkantak, Anuppur district in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The major tributaries of the Narmada are Barna, Tawa, Kanar, Kolar, Man, Hatni, Uri, Shakkar, etc.
 
• It flows westwards before falling into the Gulf of Khambhat.
 
• The Narmada river is the longest river in Madhya Pradesh and it's called "The Lifeline of Madhya Pradesh".
 
• The waterfalls created by the Narmada River include Kapil Dhara and Dudh Dhara Falls (Anuppur), Dhuandhar Falls (Bhedaghat, Jabalpur), Sahasradhara Falls (Maheshwar, Khargone), Dardhi Falls, Manadhata Falls, etc.
 
 
 
• Mahi River
 
 
• It rises in Madhya Pradesh and, after flowing through the Vagad region of Rajasthan, enters Gujarat and flows into the Arabian Sea.
 
• It is one of Five west-flowing rivers in India, along with Tapti River, Sabarmati River, Luni River (Endorheic river) and the Narmada River.
 
• Tributaries- Som, Anas, and Panam.
